```{python}
#| include: false
# the livery's fonts, style, colormaps and helpers (Make.common puts livery_mpl on PYTHONPATH
# and exports MATPLOTLIBRC, so even a deck that skips this import plots in the brand's colors)
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter
import livery_mpl
import livery_gp                     # gnuplot in the livery (livery_gp.plot())

rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)   # deterministic: CI and parity render this deck
```

# Plots

No styling code: the livery's colors, its font and the slide's type sizes come with every figure.

## Lines take the categorical slots

```{python}
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for i in range(6):
    ax.plot(x, np.sin(x + i * 0.5) + i * 0.6, label=f"Series {i + 1}")
ax.set_xlabel("Time (s)")
ax.set_ylabel("Signal")
ax.legend(ncols=2, loc="upper left")
plt.show()
```

## A seaborn bar chart from pandas

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "facility": np.repeat(["Derecho", "Casper", "Gust", "Cheyenne"], 3),
    "year": np.tile(["2024", "2025", "2026"], 4),
    "hours": [61, 72, 80, 18, 24, 31, 4, 9, 15, 40, 22, 6],
})
# a little short of the content height, for the note under it
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=livery_mpl.figsize(height=0.9))
sns.barplot(df, x="facility", y="hours", hue="year", ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.set_ylabel("Core-hours (M)")
ax.legend(title="Year", ncols=3)
plt.show()
```

::: note
Cheyenne's hours fall each year as Derecho's grow.
:::

## A stacked area in hue families

```{python}
# three groups of three: the hue names the group, its tints the members (livery_mpl.families);
# the groups are machines and the members their queues, names that promise no color
months = np.arange(1, 13)
groups = {"Derecho": ["main", "preempt", "develop"], "Casper": ["htc", "gpu", "vis"], "Gust": ["main", "gpu", "develop"]}
layers, colors, labels = [], [], []
for g, (name, queues) in enumerate(groups.items()):
    for k, queue in enumerate(queues):
        layers.append(5 + 3 * np.sin(months / 2 + g + k) + rng.uniform(0, 1.5, 12))
        colors.append(livery_mpl.families[g][k])
        labels.append(f"{name} {queue}")
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.stackplot(months, layers, colors=colors, labels=labels, alpha=livery_mpl.charts[livery_mpl.mode]["area-alpha"])
ax.set_xlim(1, 12)
ax.set_xlabel("Month")
ax.set_ylabel("Allocation (%)")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1), reverse=True)
plt.show()
```

## A heatmap on the sequential map

```{python}
hours = np.arange(24)
days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
load = 40 + 35 * np.exp(-((hours[None, :] - 14) / 5) ** 2) * np.array([1, 1, 1, 1, 0.9, 0.4, 0.3])[:, None]
load += rng.normal(0, 3, load.shape)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
im = ax.imshow(load, aspect="auto")   # the default map is the livery's (cmap "livery")
ax.set_yticks(range(7), days)
ax.set_xlabel("Hour of day")
ax.grid(False)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="Queue depth")
plt.show()
```

## A diverging field, smoothed with scipy

```{python}
field = gaussian_filter(rng.normal(0, 1, (120, 240)), sigma=9)
field /= np.abs(field).max()
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
im = ax.imshow(field, cmap="livery_div", vmin=-1, vmax=1, extent=(-180, 180, -90, 90))
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.grid(False)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="Anomaly (normalized)")
plt.show()
```

## Plots in cards

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column .card}
### Run A

```{python}
# a plot in a card takes the card's width less its pads; a shorter figure leaves room for the head
# (its own generator: the deck's rng stays the later slides')
cards = np.random.default_rng(24)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=livery_mpl.figsize("half", height=0.7))
ax.plot(np.arange(24), np.cumsum(cards.normal(0.2, 1, 24)), label="Run A")
ax.set_xlabel("Hour")
ax.set_ylabel("Drift")
plt.show()
```
:::

::: {.column .card}
### Run B

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=livery_mpl.figsize("half", height=0.7))
ax.bar(["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"], cards.integers(20, 60, 5), color=livery_mpl.colors[1])
ax.set_ylabel("Jobs")
plt.show()
```
:::

## Math in the labels

```{python}
T = np.linspace(200, 320, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for i, a in enumerate((0.5, 1.0, 2.0)):
    ax.plot(T, a * np.exp((T - 273.15) / 17), label=rf"$\alpha = {a}$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Temperature $T$ (K)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"$e_s(T) \propto \alpha\, e^{(T - T_0)/\tau}$")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

## On a dark slide {.brand-dark}

```{python}
# livery_mpl.dark(): the dark chrome and slots for a dark slide ({.brand-dark}, which every format
# draws on the livery's dark role; every slide of a dark livery)
with livery_mpl.dark():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    for i in range(4):
        ax.plot(x, np.cos(x / 2 + i) * (1 + i / 3), label=f"Member {i + 1}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Lead time (days)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Anomaly")
    ax.legend(ncols=4, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1))
    plt.show()
```

## A heavy plot as PNG

```{python}
# livery_mpl.raster(): the figures shown inside the block are PNG where the deck draws vector (the
# HTML's SVG, the PDF's PDF): a plot with thousands of marks makes a heavy SVG. The rest of the
# deck stays vector; pptx, already PNG, is unchanged. plt.show() inside the block: the format is
# picked when the figure is shown
with livery_mpl.raster():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    t = np.arange(4000)
    ax.plot(t, np.cumsum(rng.standard_normal(4000)), linewidth=0.8, label="Walk")
    ax.fill_between(t, 0, rng.random(4000) * 20 - 40, linewidth=0, alpha=0.6, label="Noise")
    ax.set_xlabel("Sample")
    ax.set_ylabel("Value")
    ax.legend(ncols=2, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1))
    plt.show()
```

## gnuplot in the livery

```{python}
# livery_gp.plot(): a gnuplot script drawn in the livery (build/livery.gp, loaded first: the
# categorical slots as linetypes, the chrome, the type sizes), the text as outlines, at the
# content area's size; the cell's last line, which Jupyter shows
livery_gp.plot("""
set xlabel 'Nodes'; set ylabel 'Time to solution (s)'
set logscale xy 2
set key top right
plot 'data/scaling.tsv' using 1:3 with linespoints title 'Solver A', \\
     '' using 1:4 with linespoints title 'Solver B', \\
     '' using 1:2 with lines dt 2 lw 2 lc rgb livery_muted title 'Ideal'
""")
```

## gnuplot on a dark slide {.brand-dark}

```{python}
# dark=True: the dark mode's colors, as livery_mpl.dark(); @livery_div, on a line of its own, the
# diverging palette
livery_gp.plot("""
@livery_div
set xlabel 'x (km)'; set ylabel 'y (km)'; set cblabel 'Anomaly'
set xrange [-3:3]; set yrange [-2:2]; set cbrange [-1:1]
set isosamples 480, 320
plot '++' using 1:2:(exp(-($1**2 + $2**2) / 3) * sin(2 * $1) * cos($2)) with image notitle
""", dark=True)
```

## ⚠︎ What breaks the style {.caution}

- `sns.set_theme()` or `plt.style.use(...)` replaces the livery's style: leave both out
- A hand-picked `figsize` changes the text size: use `livery_mpl.figsize()` (`"half"` in a column)
- A colormap by name (`viridis`) leaves the brand: `livery`, `livery_div`, `livery_seq_<ramp>`
- More than eight series: fold the rest into "Other" in `livery_mpl.muted`

## How it works

```{.python}
import livery_mpl                          # fonts, style, colormaps

fig, ax = plt.subplots()                   # the content area, slide-sized text
ax.plot(x, y)                              # the livery's categorical slots, in order
ax.imshow(z)                               # the livery's sequential map
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=livery_mpl.figsize("half"))   # one of two columns
with livery_mpl.dark():                    # a {.brand-dark} slide
    ...
with livery_mpl.raster():                  # this figure as PNG, the deck's others vector
    ...
livery_gp.plot("plot 'data.tsv' using 1:2")   # gnuplot, in the same colors and sizes
```

The styles are `build/livery.mplstyle` and `build/livery.gp`, generated with the livery's other files.
